name: Keilah
overview: Keilah was a male member of the tribe of Judah, distinguished as the Garmite and noted as the grandson of Hodiah. His identity is primarily marked by his tribal affiliation and lineage, with no additional personal details recorded. He is mentioned in the genealogical records of 1 Chronicles 4:19.
namesAndTitles: The name Keilah appears as a proper name in Scripture without a specific meaning or divine origin noted. Therefore, the name is presented plainly as it is recorded in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Keilah as the grandson of Hodiah, establishing a direct familial connection. Beyond this relationship, no further family details are provided in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Keilah's significance lies in his inclusion within the genealogical listings of the tribe of Judah, highlighting the preservation of tribal heritage and lineage. His designation as the Garmite may indicate a clan or family group within Judah, contributing to the detailed record-keeping important for understanding Israel's tribal structure. Although not a prominent figure in narrative events, his mention underscores the biblical emphasis on ancestry and God's faithfulness through generations.
